definitions.gloss: defensive position; being on the defense; defensive stance
definitions.explanation: A state of defending or being forced to react rather than take the initiative. Used in military, sports, political, and business contexts.

examples.english: To be put on the defensive.

examples.japanese: {後半|こうはん}は{守勢|しゅせい}に{立|た}たされた。
examples.english: We were forced onto the defensive in the second half.

examples.japanese: {野党|やとう}の{厳|きび}しい{追及|ついきゅう}に{対|たい}して、{政府|せいふ}は{終始|しゅうし}{守勢|しゅせい}に{回|まわ}り、{具体的|ぐたいてき}な{回答|かいとう}を{避|さ}けた。
examples.english: Facing harsh questioning from the opposition, the government remained on the defensive throughout and avoided giving concrete answers.

notes:
A compound of {守|しゅ} (defense, to guard) and {勢|せい} (force, posture). Almost always appears in the phrase {守勢|しゅせい}に{回|まわ}る (to be put on the defensive) or {守勢|しゅせい}に{立|た}つ (to take a defensive stance). The opposite is {攻勢|こうせい} (offensive).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {守勢|しゅせい}に{回|まわ}る: to be on the defensive
- {守勢|しゅせい}に{立|た}たされる: to be forced onto the defensive
- {守勢|しゅせい}に{立|た}つ: to take a defensive position
- {終始|しゅうし}{守勢|しゅせい}: on the defensive throughout

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {攻勢|こうせい}: offensive — the opposite, taking the initiative to attack or push forward
- {防衛|ぼうえい}: defense — broader term for defense, especially national defense
- {受|う}け{身|み}: passive, reactive — a general term for being in a reactive position
